title: Handoff Simulation with Hysteresis
aim: Simulate a mobile moving between two base stations and study how hysteresis affects handoff and ping-pong counts.
parameters: BS1 at 0 m; BS2 at 2000 m
Mobile positions 10 m to 1995 m in 5 m steps
Reference RSS P0 = -30 dBm at 1 m; path-loss exponent n = 3.5
Gaussian shadowing standard deviation = 4 dB; random seed = 7
method: Calculate each base station's RSS using P0 - 10*n*log10(distance) plus seeded Gaussian shadowing. Switch the serving cell only when the candidate RSS exceeds the current RSS by the hysteresis margin. Count handoffs and extra handoffs as ping-pongs.
result: The simulation produces 35 handoffs with no hysteresis and only 1 with a 10 dB margin. Increasing hysteresis suppresses rapid ping-pong switching, while delaying the one necessary handoff. With a 6 dB margin, the fixed-seed run produces 7 handoffs.
